survey: Watch the full video. Mark gameplay, non-game footage and end cards. Choose as few segments as possible, up to 30 seconds each, with cuts near movement starts or camera changes. List scenes, characters, objects and their first clear appearances.
frames: Choose the fewest clear frames covering this segment's scenes, characters, objects and ground, especially newly appearing items. Select existing generated references for content already seen. When inspecting a converted image, compare every logo and all text with its source. Logos and text must remain unchanged in content, lettering, font, color, shape, size, placement and appearance, including numbers, brand marks, warnings and HUD labels. Return ok=false and describe the discrepancy if any are restyled, made realistic, embossed, distorted, replaced, added or removed, even when realistic material coverage is complete.
image: Convert Image 1 to realistic materials, matching the references' style, color, brightness, shadows and texture. Preserve every logo and all text from Image 1 unchanged, including numbers, brand marks, warnings and HUD labels. Keep their exact content, lettering, font, color, shape, size, placement and original appearance. Exclude them from material conversion, realistic restyling, relighting and embossing.
video: Edit the video: replace its materials to match the reference images. Preserve every logo and all text from the source video unchanged at each corresponding time, including numbers, brand marks, warnings and HUD labels. Keep their exact content, lettering, font, color, shape, size, placement, original appearance and source-timed changes. Exclude them from material conversion, realistic restyling, relighting and embossing; use the source video as their authority even if a reference image differs.
segment: Compare the result with the source, judging the overall impression at normal playback speed. Allow a small number of subtle defects, brief minor clipping, small shape or texture inconsistencies and other imperfections that ordinary viewers are unlikely to notice in motion. Do not use paused frames, magnification or close frame-by-frame inspection as the acceptance standard for scene materials and action. Report missed realistic materials, content changes, motion changes or artifacts when readily noticeable during normal playback or when they materially change the main content or action. Ignore issues already present in the source. Strict exception: every logo and all text must remain unchanged from the source at each corresponding time, including numbers, brand marks, warnings and HUD labels. Compare content, lettering, font, color, shape, size, placement, original appearance and source-timed changes. Report any restyling, realistic conversion, relighting, embossing, blur, ghosting, deformation, substitution, addition or removal affecting logos or text as an issue and fail the segment. Inspect source-matched stills when needed to verify them. The minor-defect tolerance does not apply to logos or text. Other UI and HUD graphics retain the relaxed motion standard: tolerate mild blur, ghosting or jelly-like deformation during changes if static appearance is normal and placement remains stable; report obvious drift, severe distortion, persistent static defects or major missing or added elements. Return pass with an empty issues list only when no unresolved issue remains.
tail: Compare Image 1 (the previous generated segment last frame) with Image 2 (the next source segment first frame). Decide only whether these are consecutive views of the same continuous shot. Ignore differences in material realism, texture quality, lighting style and rendering style. Return ok=true for the same continuous shot, otherwise false. List inventory IDs visible in Image 1 without judging materials.
